The bug is in src/core.mjs: `out.push(!x||t>x.end?null:x.v)`. The contract says a key is absent when `now >= putTime + ttl`, but `t>x.end` incorrectly returns the value at the exact expiration time.

A smallest counterexample uses two operations: `solve([[0,"put","a",7,1],[1,"get","a"]])`. The put sets `end = 1`; at the get, `1 > 1` is false, so the actual result is `[7]`. The required result is `[null]`, because `1 >= 1`. No implementation changes made.

This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript project that simulates a time-limited key-value cache and returns lookup results, using null for misses.

The architecture has two layers: src/service.mjs exposes execute, which delegates to the synchronous solve(ops) function in src/core.mjs. The core processes operations sequentially, storing values and expiration timestamps in a Map and collecting get results; a Node test checks the service entry point.

There’s an expiration-boundary bug: the specification says a key expires when time is greater than or equal to its expiry, but the implementation checks only greater than, so it incorrectly returns the value at the exact expiration time.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript project implementing a time-limited key-value cache. Its synchronous API, `solve(ops)`, processes put and get operations in input order and returns get results, using `null` for missing or expired keys.

`src/core.mjs` contains the logic, storing values and expiration timestamps in a `Map`; the current version treats a key as expired when `time >= expiration`. `src/service.mjs` exposes a thin `execute` wrapper, and `tests/smoke.test.mjs` checks that entry point using Node’s built-in test runner (`npm test`).
